items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (restoreState, normalizeRestoredQueryState, reconcileRestoredQueryState), but the long normalize/reconcile logic has few comments and leans on casts like `(rawData as any).pages ?? (stateData as any)?.pages`. All restore code is crammed into query.ts.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: reconcileRestoredQueryState spans about query.ts:868-993 (~125 lines), which breaks the 100-line cap. Internal helpers are exported publicly. There is no separate persister.ts. Vue useBaseQuery and useQueries were changed even though adapters should need no changes. A #restoredFromPersister flag is spread across many methods.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Restored counts and timestamps are not checked for valid values. Public signatures use `QueryOptions<any, any, any, any>` and `as any` casts. Promise-piggyback handling had to be patched in several places with `.then(isPersisterRestoreResult ? ... )`. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult({data,state}) is exported from query-core, and the marker is a Symbol.for brand. fetch() catches the marker and calls restoreState, so no success dispatch or callbacks run. Bulk restoreQueries reuses restoreState with {reconcile:true}, so both paths share it. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Persisters that return plain data still take the normal success path, and the new exports only add to the API. However, Vue useBaseQuery and useQueries now always subscribe in the non-restoring branch, and fetch() wraps the retryer promise in a new `.then`. These shift internal behavior beyond the persister path.
